source_name: CBCG – Register of banks (per-bank entity records, EN + ME)
why_relevant: Regulator-maintained register giving the authoritative current list of Montenegrin banks, their foreign parents and licensed status — the actor map this cell needs to keep the foreign-parent watchlist complete as ownership changes (Hipotekarna→AikGroup, Addiko→possible NLB).

source_name: CBCG – Saopštenja (press releases), incl. meetings with foreign-parent bank managements
why_relevant: CBCG press releases name the attending management of foreign-owned banks (e.g. a meeting with Ziraat Bank Montenegro listing board president, deputy, CEO and executive director by name) — an indirect but precisely dated way to observe who currently holds which seat at a foreign subsidiary.

source_name: CKB (Crnogorska komercijalna banka) – Top management and Supervisory Board page
why_relevant: The local mirror of OTP group decisions: the roster page that changes when OTP appoints a new CKB CEO or board member. English version available, making diff-based detection cheap and unambiguous.

source_name: MarketScreener – company/board profiles for Montenegrin subsidiaries and parents
why_relevant: Third-party aggregator maintaining structured board/manager lists for NLB Banka a.d. Podgorica (MEMONBRA1PG2) and the parent groups; useful for change-detection and for resolving officer names/roles when primary sites are stale.

source_name: LinkedIn – Erste Group / NLB Group / OTP company job feeds
why_relevant: Group company pages carry Montenegro-located vacancies and self-reported role changes by executives, which frequently predate any official announcement of a leadership move.

source_name: CBCG — Registar platnih institucija i njihovih agenata (Register of payment institutions and their agents)
why_relevant: Authoritative, legally mandated actor list for the entire Montenegrin non-bank payments employer universe. Fetched content named 7 licensed PIs: MONTENEGRO TRANSFERS DOO, CAPITAL TRANSFER MNE DOO, MONETA MNE DOO, PAYSPOT ME DOO, ALTA PAY GROUP DOO, PRESTOPAY DOO, and Business Integration and Business Intelligence d.o.o. (all Podgorica). Each entry links a per-institution PDF that carries legal name, address and licensed service scope — the seed set from which all hiring/leadership tracking in this cell derives. Agent sub-registers also reveal distribution-network expansion, a leading indicator of field-staff hiring.

source_name: CBCG — Registar institucija za elektronski novac i njihovih agenata (E-money institutions register)
why_relevant: The definitive EMI actor list. On fetch it stated the register currently contains no entered e-money institution ('U Registru trenutno nema upisane institucije za elektronski novac'). That is itself high-value intelligence: the EMI segment in Montenegro is empty, so any first entry is a market-entry event that will be immediately followed by country-manager/compliance-officer hiring. Worth monitoring precisely because it is a zero-state that will change.

source_name: CBCG — Registar platnih sistema (Register of payment systems / system operators)
why_relevant: Identifies licensed payment-system operators in Montenegro — the infrastructure layer employers (clearing/settlement operators) distinct from PIs. The page publishes a 'Pregled registra' PDF; the HTML body itself carried no names in my fetch, so the operator list lives inside the PDF and must be pulled from there.

source_name: CBCG — Spisak platnih institucija i institucija za elektronski novac kojima je oduzeto odobrenje (revoked-licence list)
why_relevant: Licence withdrawal is the strongest possible org-change signal for a payments employer: it precedes or accompanies wind-down, mass departures and talent release into the market. Complements the positive registers by capturing exits, which registers of live entities silently drop.

source_name: CBCG — Pružaoci finansijskih usluga / kontrolna funkcija (supervised financial service providers hub)
why_relevant: Supervisory hub that aggregates the categories of supervised entities and typically routes to licensing decisions. CBCG approves 'fit and proper' persons for management bodies of payment institutions, so licensing/approval decisions published under the supervisory function are a primary route to named leadership appointments — the highest-value item for this cell's leadership-moves topic.

source_name: Bankar.me — Oglasi za posao (financial-sector job-ads category)
why_relevant: Single highest-yield hiring source found for this cell. Bankar.me is the Montenegrin banking/finance trade portal and it republishes payment-institution vacancies verbatim — a confirmed example is 'Platna institucija PaySpot ME doo Podgorica otvara više pozicija: Regionalni menadžer prodaje za regije Sjever, Jug i Centralnu regiju', which reveals both headcount growth and a three-region field-sales org structure. It also runs director-level ads ('Direktor sektora...', 'zapošljava Izvršnog direktora'), covering the leadership-moves topic.

source_name: Bankar.me — employer/vendor tag feeds (e.g. 'payten oglasi za posao')
why_relevant: Bankar.me maintains per-employer tag archives, giving a ready-made per-actor hiring timeline. The existence of a dedicated Payten tag confirms the card-processing vendor recruits into the Montenegrin market through this channel. The same tag pattern can be constructed for each PI in the CBCG register, turning one portal into an actor-indexed hiring monitor.

source_name: PaySpot ME d.o.o. Podgorica — corporate site
why_relevant: Licensed payment institution positioning itself as the payments-services leader in Montenegro and demonstrably in an expansion phase (multi-region sales-manager recruitment). Its own site is the primary channel for career pages, location-network growth and management presentation. Parent group PaySpot d.o.o. Novi Sad adds a cross-border talent and management-transfer dimension.

source_name: PrestoPay d.o.o. Podgorica — corporate site and blog
why_relevant: Licensed PI that publicly claims to be the first payment institution licensed for payment services in Montenegro under a PSD2-aligned framework, and runs a consumer mobile app. Its blog is an active corporate-communications channel where product launches, compliance milestones and (by extension) team/leadership announcements appear. App-led PIs scale engineering and compliance headcount fastest.

source_name: Moneta MNE d.o.o. Podgorica — corporate site (MoneyGram representative)
why_relevant: Licensed PI and the MoneyGram representative in Montenegro, described as a leading non-bank financial institution specialised in fast money transfer. Money-remitter employers hire branch and agent-network staff continuously, and their principal-brand relationship (MoneyGram) means principal-driven org changes propagate locally. Site carries contact and management-facing pages.

source_name: Montenegro Transfers d.o.o. Podgorica — corporate site (Western Union agent, Altapay Group)
why_relevant: Licensed PI acting as Western Union agent for send/receive in Montenegro, and — per the site's own branding — part of Altapay Group, which also owns the separately licensed ALTA PAY GROUP DOO. That group linkage is a material org-structure finding: two register entries, one ownership cluster, so leadership moves at one may be group-level. Also runs an active Facebook page used for announcements.

source_name: ALTA PAY GROUP d.o.o. Podgorica — company profile (CompanyWall ME)
why_relevant: Commercial business-registry aggregator that exposes exactly the fields this cell needs per actor: named director, owner, registered activity code, address, founding date and employee headcount. For ALTA PAY GROUP it reported director Maja Armenko, owner Davor Macura, activity 6419, registered Bul. Ivana Crnojevića 54/3 Podgorica since 28 Oct 2019, and roughly 8 employees. Headcount plus director fields make it a direct proxy for both hiring trajectory and leadership change across every PI in the register.

source_name: CRPS — Centralna evidencija stvarnih vlasnika (beneficial-ownership register)
why_relevant: Beneficial-ownership filings expose the real control structure behind PIs — critical here because the Montenegro Transfers / Alta Pay Group cluster and foreign-parented PIs (PaySpot ME under a Novi Sad parent) mean apparent org changes are often group-driven. Ownership shifts reliably precede management replacement.

source_name: Zavod za zapošljavanje Crne Gore (ZZZCG) — Oglasi / slobodna radna mjesta
why_relevant: The national employment agency's vacancy database is the legally-routed channel for Montenegrin employers, giving near-complete coverage of formally advertised roles including back-office and branch positions at PIs and remitters that never reach commercial job boards. Postings carry structured employer, role and location fields, and are also published in the daily 'Dan' on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays.

source_name: Payten / Asseco SEE — Montenegro operations and careers
why_relevant: Fills the card-acquiring/processing half of this cell, which the CBCG PI register does not cover. Payten (Asseco SEE group) supplies processing, ATM/POS and e-commerce services and maintains a Montenegro office at Svetlane Kane Redevic 3, Podgorica (+382 20 651 951), with roughly 1,500 staff group-wide. It is the most likely local employer of card-processing and terminal-services staff, and Asseco SEE's group structure/contacts pages let one confirm the Montenegrin legal entity.

source_name: Radnik.me — Montenegrin job board
why_relevant: Commercial aggregator of Montenegrin vacancies with location filtering (a Podgorica-specific view exists, matching where every licensed PI is registered). Useful for catching PI and agent-network roles posted commercially rather than via ZZZCG, and for measuring hiring velocity over time.

source_name: Zaposli.me — Montenegrin/regional job portal
why_relevant: Self-described as among the most visited employment sites in Montenegro and the region. Regional reach matters for this cell because several PIs are subsidiaries of Serbian groups (PaySpot, Alta), so cross-border postings can signal Montenegrin team build-outs staffed from the parent market.

source_name: Prekoveze.me — Montenegrin job board
why_relevant: Additional Montenegrin vacancy portal ('Poslovi u Crnoj Gori') providing redundancy against single-board coverage gaps. In a market this small, any given PI vacancy may appear on only one board, so breadth across boards materially raises recall.

source_name: Posao.crna.gora.me — job ads plus business directory (Poslovni adresar)
why_relevant: Dual-purpose: a vacancy feed and a Montenegrin business directory ('Poslovni adresar') indexed by city. The directory half helps resolve PI addresses, branch presence and sibling entities, supporting actor-map maintenance as much as hiring capture.

source_name: Pazar3.me — classifieds, jobs section
why_relevant: High-traffic general classifieds carrying a jobs vertical. Relevant mainly for the agent/retail layer of the payments ecosystem — payment-point operators and cash-in/cash-out agents recruit counter staff here rather than through formal boards, which is a leading indicator of network expansion by the PIs behind them.

source_name: Pošta Crne Gore — money transfer services (postal payment operator)
why_relevant: The national post is a large-scale non-bank money-transfer distribution employer in Montenegro, operating inbound/outbound remittance services through its branch network. It is not in the PI register (postal operators are treated separately) but competes directly with the licensed remitters for the same counter workforce, and its own recruitment and org changes shape that labour pool.

source_name: Poslovi Infostud — regional (RS) employer profiles for ME-linked payment groups
why_relevant: Serbia's dominant job portal hosts employer profiles for the parent groups of Montenegrin PIs (ALTA PAY GROUP DOO BEOGRAD, PaySpot Novi Sad). Group-level hiring and management pages there frequently disclose expansion into Montenegro before anything appears locally, making it an early-warning channel for this cell despite being an out-of-country source.
